Subject: Post-call recap & follow-ups: pricing metrics and usage sample

Alex - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have a shared next step list:

- Goal: understand your production token volumes and budget targets so we can recommend an optimized serving profile (model flavor, batching, caching).
- Action items for you: share a representative API usage sample (request/response sizes, average generated tokens, peak QPS). I attached a CSV (AcmeHealth_API_usage.csv) with a suggested template - feel free to paste a sample export.
- Specific questions you flagged on the call that I want to clarify in writing:
  1) Do you track usage as tokens, characters, or requests today?
  2) Do you have a target $/1M tokens (ballpark is fine) or a monthly budget range we should optimize for?
  3) How much prompt reuse do you expect (i.e., percentage of queries that are identical or share a common prefix)?

A couple notes up front to set expectations:
- Our pricing and cost modeling use tokens as the billing unit (input + output tokens). Characters and requests are useful proxies but don't map 1:1 to billed tokens.
- Redis-style prompt caching or prefix caching can materially reduce model compute and cost when we can serve from cache (no model call), but only cached responses avoid billed inference tokens entirely. If caching only reduces generation compute (e.g., faster KV-cache replay) but still requires a model pass, tokens are still billed.

If you can send the CSV and any rough budget targets, I'll run a quick cost projection and share two scenarios (conservative/high-efficiency) by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks - Ben

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & follow-ups: pricing metrics and usage sample

Alex - great data, thanks for sending that over. Below is a concise explainer and a quick back-of-envelope cost calc so your procurement team has numbers for budgeting.

1) Tokens vs characters vs requests
- Tokens are the billing unit we use: billed tokens = input tokens + output tokens processed by the model.
- Characters are a raw client-side metric (bytes/characters in your logs). There isn't a fixed conversion but a general rule-of-thumb is ~4 characters per token for English text, so 120M input characters ~ 30M input tokens (very rough). Variability is high for code / multilingual text.
- Requests count API calls and are useful for QPS/throughput; they do not directly map to billed tokens because one request can contain many tokens or very few.

2) Prompt caching vs billed tokens
- If a request is served entirely from a server-side cache (we return a stored response without invoking the model), there is no model inference and therefore no billed tokens for that request. This is the biggest cost saver.
- If we use prefix/KV caching inside the runtime to avoid recomputing earlier layers but still run the model for the tail, billing depends on whether the model was executed for those tokens. In practice:
  - Pure cache hit (identical prompt/response): 0 billed tokens.
  - Partial reuse (shared context/prefix): you may still be billed for the non-cached portion - savings depend on how much of the sequence is avoided.
- We can implement a cache policy that returns cached responses for high-reuse templates (common for templated help responses) and falls back to live inference otherwise.

3) Example unit economics (using your rough numbers)
- Your reported characters -> rough tokens: (120M input chars + 40M output chars) / 4 ~ 40M tokens/month (simplified).
- At your procurement target: $15-$25 per 1M tokens => monthly cost range ~ $600-$1,000.
- At incumbent rate $35/1M tokens => ~ $1,400/month.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll run a more precise conversion using the attached CSV and estimate cache-hit scenarios (e.g., 20% pure cache hits, 50% partial reuse) and share a conservative and high-efficiency cost model.
- Marissa, can we schedule a 30-min technical deep dive next week to go over prefix caching and integration details with Acme's logs?

If this looks directionally right for procurement, happy to put an initial commercial proposal together (term sheet + SOW).

Thanks - Ben
